findings.text: The doc that describes the processes still lists the old steps: `public/framework/core/Task/doc/process.md:5` and `:69` say build is "… execute → review → merge", and `:70` says design is "… code → review → merge". Neither mentions the new `index` step. Add it to all three lines in this branch, because Law 9 says the doc must match the code.

This diff completes none of the numbered items in requirements.md. It adds an `index` step to both process templates (`BuildProcess.js`, `DesignProcess.js`) and a "show the look first" sentence to the build plan step. At most it is part of item 4 ("a builder that builds a whole system documents it"). Item 4's real deliverables are still to do: the unified docs rule, written into the documentation skill, `ai/doc/readme-system.md` and the mastermind role readme. Don't count this diff as item 4 done.

`index` is a safe step id. Nothing named `index` exists on Task, Process or Item (I checked Task.js, Process.js and Item.js), so it won't call a verb by accident, which is what the warning at `BuildProcess.js:2` is about.

The test covers only the build template: `Servex/ProcessRunner.test.mjs:55,133` now expect 8 steps, and line 80 completes `index`. Nothing tests the design template's new step. A one-line check that `design` has `index` between `code` and `review` would catch a template that drifts later.

Is there a simpler way? Not really. A separate step written into each template is the plainest way to do it. The same `do` text appears in both templates (`BuildProcess.js` index step, `DesignProcess.js` index step), so if it changes often, one shared constant would avoid two copies drifting apart. That is optional.
